In order to install Raid on Mint you'll need 3 hard drives. It's an inconvenient process but it works. Connect a single hard drive that will not be used as a Raid device into SATA Port 1 on your motherboard. Connect your CD Rom to SATA 3 on the motherboard.

Boot Mint from CD and install it on the single drive. Once it's done shutdown. Do not update Mint as you don't want add time to your Raid configuration time in case something goes wrong.

[Make sure your computer is off.] Disconnect SATA 3 from the CD Rom and plug it into your first Raid Disk 1. Connect SATA 2 to Raid Disk 2. Leave the single drive with Mint installed on it on SATA 1. You'll be running temporarily without a CD Rom.

After all connections are made Bootup.

Load Terminal

sudo apt-get update

sudo apt-get install gedit

sudo apt-get install gparted

Under GPartition you should see 3 drives. Under every system it should be different. For example SDB may be your Mint Drive and SDA and SDC may be your 2 Raid Drives.

Select one of your Raid drives for example SDA and create a Linux Swap partition that is 1.5x to 2x your system RAM. Make sure to select Linux_Swap on the dropdown menu for this partition. The remaining partition use the entire amount as UNFORMATTED. Now do the same for your 2nd Raid drive with a Linux Swap and Unformatted partition. Click the APPLY ALL OPTIONS arrow at the top to process your configuration.

Afterward right click on each Unformated partition select Manage Flags and set them to RAID. Exit gparted.

Open Terminal

sudo apt-get install mdadm

Create Raid

sudo mdadm --create /dev/md0 --level=0 --raid-devices=2 /dev/sd[ac]2 <------ A and C is the raid devices for mine. Check your system it may be different. 2 at the end is the partition for mine. They may be different for you. Again check your system under gparted it may be in a different partition.

sudo sh -c "mdadm -Ds >> /etc/mdadm/mdadm.conf"

Make swap and Raid

sudo mkswap /dev/sda1 <---- Check gparted for your exact drive you set to swap it could be sda2 or something else

sudo mkswap /dev/sdc1 <----- Check gparted again for your 2nd swap drive it could be sdc2 or something else

sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/md0

Copy Mint to Raid

sudo mount /dev/md0 /mnt

sudo rsync -vax / /mnt/

Now here is the tricky part after the copy part is done. You need to edit the UUID for each drive.

sudo blkid

sudo gedit /mnt/etc/fstab

Under fstab file copy and paste another SWAP line below. The UUID for your Raid will be contained in blkid under /dev/md0 Copy this UUID to fstab file [DO NOT COPY THE UUID for each single RAID DRIVE. You want to use the md0 UUID]. Copy the UUID from the blkid info to fstab for both your SWAP partitions you created as well. Save fstab file and exit gedit.

for i in /dev /dev/pts /proc /sys; do sudo mount -B $i /mnt$i; done

sudo chroot /mnt

update-initramfs -u

dpkg-reconfigure grub-pc

exit

for i in /dev/pts /dev /proc /sys; do sudo umount /mnt$i; done

Shutdown computer. Disconnect SATA 1 from single drive. Disconnect SATA 3 from Raid Disk 1. Connect SATA 1 to Raid Disk 1 and connect SATA 3 back to your CD Rom. Bootup and enjoy Raid 0.
